label: In every possible history, each moment with a contingent concrete thing present has a founded past
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, attribution deferred: in every history accessible from the selected world, every moment at which some contingent concrete individual is present has a founded past (Acc of the strict order of moments: no strictly descending sequence of moments below it). It denies horn H2, a non-well-founded populated past, for every accessible history in which a contingent concrete thing is present at all; histories with no contingent concrete thing present are unconstrained. H2 covers an endless past AND a dense past with a first moment: on non-negative rational times every moment after 0 has t, t/2, t/4, ... below it. So this premise forbids a contingent concrete thing to be present at any non-initial moment of a dense-time history in any accessible world: an anti-continuum commitment (control 8). It is not a claim that time has a first moment, nor a metric finitude claim, and it mentions no cause.
